# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

🚨 **IMPORTANT: docs matrix misstates the shipped behavior for "Linux (no user namespaces)"**

This row (and the prose at `docs/cubes.md:224-226`, which lists "Linux without
user namespaces" among "hosts without an enforcing backend") does not match the
implementation:

- `LinuxUnshareBackend.enforces` is statically `true` (`linux_unshare.dart:44`)
  and `osName` is always `Platform.operatingSystem` — there is no user-namespace
  capability probe. On a userns-less Linux host, `backend: kernel` **binds the
  kernel run** and every exec hard-fails as a launch failure
  (`fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unshare failed: ...`), not the clean
  "backend: kernel is not available on this platform … set spec.allowDegrade"
  refusal this row promises.
- Worse, the `+ allowDegrade: true` cell — "policy (+ loud warning)" — cannot
  happen: `allowDegrade` only applies when `_kernelRunFor` returns null
  (`sandboxed_shell.dart:203-214`), and on Linux it never does. The PR's own
  description states the correct rule ("launch failures are not degrade … the
  opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case"); the table contradicts
  both the code and the PR prose.

An operator on a userns-less Linux CI container (common, per the test note in
`linux_unshare.dart`) reading this matrix would expect `allowDegrade: true` to
yield a working policy-mode run; instead every command errors. Since the
platform × spec × fallback matrix is an explicit AC of this PR, please fix
before merge — either:

1. correct the row/prose to "hard error (unshare EPERM) — launch failures are
   never degraded, even with `allowDegrade: true`", or
2. make the docs true by adding a user-namespace capability probe so a
   userns-less Linux really refuses (clean `allowDegrade`-naming error) /
   degrades under the opt-in.

Option 1 is the minimal fix consistent with the stated design rule; option 2
changes runtime behavior and deserves its own issue.

🚨 **IMPORTANT: builtin presets have no `allowDegrade` escape hatch — on Windows/web every preset now refuses all commands**

Every builtin preset generates `backend: kernel` with no `allowDegrade`
(`cube_presets.dart:150`), and there is no CLI surface to opt in
(`/cube use <preset>` → `maybeSpec` builds the manifest verbatim). With the new
kernel-or-refuse rule created at this line, a preset user on Windows, web, or
any host without an enforcing backend (or without `HOME` set) goes from
"works in policy mode with a loud warning" (previous behavior) to **every
command refused** — the only remedy is hand-writing a custom manifest that
duplicates the preset and adds `allowDegrade: true`.

The hardening itself is right (SEC-05), but the opt-in the refusal message
recommends (`set spec.allowDegrade: true`) is unreachable for preset users.
Please address at least one of:

1. Document the preset consequence in `docs/cubes.md`'s preset section (the new
   matrix doesn't mention presets at all) and in the refusal path when the
   active spec came from a preset.
2. Add a first-class opt-in: a preset variant (e.g. `l1-core-degrade`), a
   `/cube use <preset> --allow-degrade` flag, or a generated-manifest override
   — so the fix the error message names is actually available.

Also worth noting: `SandboxedShell.prepare` changed `Future<String>` →
`Future<String?>` and the refusal/passthrough semantics are new; both are
public API via `lib/src/cube/cube.dart` — fine for this repo, but worth a line
in the release notes since external hosts may call `prepare()` directly.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 815
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/815
- **Title**: fix(cube): backend kernel means kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit allowDegrade (#793)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-793` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +780
- **Deletions**: -150
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:58:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T23:13:13Z

## PR Description

## SEC-05 - `backend: kernel` is kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit `allowDegrade`

Closes #793. Stacked on #803 (SEC-02, same subsystem).

### Before
A `backend: kernel` spec on a host without an enforcing backend (Windows, web, Linux without user namespaces) **silently degraded to policy mode** - the requested isolation level was a wish, not a contract.

### After
- **Refuse by default.** Undeliverable kernel spec -> every `exec` and every background job answers a clean, stable `fa_cube[<name>]: backend: kernel is not available on this platform ... set spec.allowDegrade: true to allow the degrade` error. **Zero commands run**, zero staging writes, no wrapper is ever reached.
- **Explicit degrade.** `allowDegrade: true` in the manifest is the only path to policy mode; it fires `onDegrade` (loud `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unavailable, running in policy mode`), and the effective mode is queryable afterwards via `SandboxedShell.effectiveBackend` / `SandboxedExecutionEnv.effectiveBackend` (`null` = passthrough or refused; `policy` = degradaded or default; `kernel` = OS-wrapped).
- **Launch failures are not degrade.** A missing `sandbox-exec`/`unshare` or an EPERM/SBPL refusal on an *enforcing* platform stays a hard spawn error regardless of `allowDegrade` - the opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case.
- **Config surface.** `CubeSpec.allowDegrade` (default `false`), strict boolean parse, canonical map omits it when `false` (cache keys byte-identical), `schema/cube_schema.json` + `docs/cubes.md` document it; docs gain the platform x spec x fallback matrix.

### Acceptance (issue #793)
- **AC1** `kernel_spec_on_unsupported_platform_is_refused` - `test/cube/runtime/sandboxed_shell_test.dart` AC1 tests (windows / no-os / no-home: refusal names allowDegrade, inner shell never reached) + env-level background-job refusal.
- **AC2** `allow_degrade_runs_queryable` - AC2 test: degrading spec runs in policy mode, `onDegrade` fired, `effectiveBackend() == policy`; forward test on the env.
- **AC3** REG property test - AC3 "explicit kernel never silently executes in policy mode" across the os x allowDegrade matrix (macos/linux/windows/null): every outcome is kernel-wrapped, refused-with-reason, or explicitly-degraded-and-loud.
- Docs matrix: `docs/cubes.md` "spec.backend" (platform x spec -> kernel/policy/refusal).

`dart analyze lib/src/cube test/cube` clean; `test/cube` green apart from the 3 pre-existing live-leg failures proven identical on the pristine base (see #803): 315 passed / 3 skipped.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

This row (and the prose at `docs/cubes.md:224-226`, which lists "Linux without
user namespaces" among "hosts without an enforcing backend") does not match the
implementation:

- `LinuxUnshareBackend.enforces` is statically `true` (`linux_unshare.dart:44`)
  and `osName` is always `Platform.operatingSystem` — there is no user-namespace
  capability probe. On a userns-less Linux host, `backend: kernel` **binds the
  kernel run** and every exec hard-fails as a launch failure
  (`fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unshare failed: ...`), not the clean
  "backend: kernel is not available on this platform … set spec.allowDegrade"
  refusal this row promises.
- Worse, the `+ allowDegrade: true` cell — "policy (+ loud warning)" — cannot
  happen: `allowDegrade` only applies when `_kernelRunFor` returns null
  (`sandboxed_shell.dart:203-214`), and on Linux it never does. The PR's own
  description states the correct rule ("launch failures are not degrade … the
  opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case"); the table contradicts
  both the code and the PR prose.

An operator on a userns-less Linux CI container (common, per the test note in
`linux_unshare.dart`) reading this matrix would expect `allowDegrade: true` to
yield a working policy-mode run; instead every command errors. Since the
platform × spec × fallback matrix is an explicit AC of this PR, please fix
before merge — either:

1. correct the row/prose to "hard error (unshare EPERM) — launch failures are
   never degraded, even with `allowDegrade: true`", or
2. make the docs true by adding a user-namespace capability probe so a
   userns-less Linux really refuses (clean `allowDegrade`-naming error) /
   degrades under the opt-in.

Option 1 is the minimal fix consistent with the stated design rule; option 2
changes runtime behavior and deserves its own issue.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/cube_preset_refuse_no_optin.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: builtin presets have no `allowDegrade` escape hatch — on Windows/web every preset now refuses all commands**

Every builtin preset generates `backend: kernel` with no `allowDegrade`
(`cube_presets.dart:150`), and there is no CLI surface to opt in
(`/cube use <preset>` → `maybeSpec` builds the manifest verbatim). With the new
kernel-or-refuse rule created at this line, a preset user on Windows, web, or
any host without an enforcing backend (or without `HOME` set) goes from
"works in policy mode with a loud warning" (previous behavior) to **every
command refused** — the only remedy is hand-writing a custom manifest that
duplicates the preset and adds `allowDegrade: true`.

The hardening itself is right (SEC-05), but the opt-in the refusal message
recommends (`set spec.allowDegrade: true`) is unreachable for preset users.
Please address at least one of:

1. Document the preset consequence in `docs/cubes.md`'s preset section (the new
   matrix doesn't mention presets at all) and in the refusal path when the
   active spec came from a preset.
2. Add a first-class opt-in: a preset variant (e.g. `l1-core-degrade`), a
   `/cube use <preset> --allow-degrade` flag, or a generated-manifest override
   — so the fix the error message names is actually available.

Also worth noting: `SandboxedShell.prepare` changed `Future<String>` →
`Future<String?>` and the refusal/passthrough semantics are new; both are
public API via `lib/src/cube/cube.dart` — fine for this repo, but worth a line
in the release notes since external hosts may call `prepare()` directly.
"}

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failed rename leaks the temp profile file**

When `writeFile(tmp)` succeeds but `renamePath(tmp, profilePath)` fails, the
`.tmp` file is left behind and never cleaned up; the next attempt derives a new
name via `_tmpSeq++`, so repeated staging failures (e.g. a read-only staging
directory that intermittently accepts writes, or a planted directory at
`profilePath` making every rename fail with `EISDIR`/`ENOTEMPTY`) accumulate
`~/.fah/cube-profiles/<hash>.<id>-<n>.tmp` files indefinitely.

Consider deleting the temp file (or reusing the same temp name) on the rename
failure path:

```dart
if (rename.isErr) {
  await fs.remove(tmp, force: true); // best-effort cleanup
  stagingError = 'profile staging failed: ${rename.errorOrNull!.message}';
  return false;
}
```

Pure hygiene — the fail-closed semantics are correct as written.

💡 **SUGGESTION: unrelated change bundled — `.pub-cache/` in `.gitignore`**

`.pub-cache/` has nothing to do with SEC-05/SEC-02 or the cube subsystem; it
looks like a local development environment artifact (`dart pub get` with a
repo-local cache) that slipped into the branch. Harmless, but it makes the diff
noisier and will linger in `main` forever. Prefer dropping it here (or moving
it to a local/global git exclude, `git config core.excludesFile`) and keeping
this PR purely on the ticket scope — if it's genuinely needed for CI, call it
out in the PR description.

## PR Description

## SEC-05 - `backend: kernel` is kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit `allowDegrade`

Closes #793. Stacked on #803 (SEC-02, same subsystem).

### Before
A `backend: kernel` spec on a host without an enforcing backend (Windows, web, Linux without user namespaces) **silently degraded to policy mode** - the requested isolation level was a wish, not a contract.

### After
- **Refuse by default.** Undeliverable kernel spec -> every `exec` and every background job answers a clean, stable `fa_cube[<name>]: backend: kernel is not available on this platform ... set spec.allowDegrade: true to allow the degrade` error. **Zero commands run**, zero staging writes, no wrapper is ever reached.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

So even a policy-DENIED command returns the refusal error instead of the standard exit-127 `Ok` result. This is intentional per PR description ("every exec ... answers a clean, stable error"). OK.

5. Now a REAL potential correctness issue: `startupFailure()` when `kernel != null` and probed — `if (kernel.probed) return kernel.failureNote;`. First call: `kernel.probed = true; if (!await kernel.stageVerified()) {...}`. Then it runs the wrapped `true` probe through `_inner.exec` — that RUNS A COMMAND (`sandbox-exec -f profile true`). But wait — the startup probe runs `kernel.backend.wrapCommand('true', ...)` — the raw wrapped `true` command, executed via `_inner.exec` WITHOUT the policy engine check. This is a hard-coded `true` no-op, fine by design (documented "runs a wrapped no-op command once per spec first").

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: `startupFailure()` doesn't check `_refusal` before `kernel.probed` — it does: refusal checked before kernel. Good.

6. Another potential issue: in `SandboxedExecutionEnv.startShellJob`, for a refused spec the policy check runs first: `engine.checkCommand(command)`. If the command is policy-DENIED, the user gets the policy denial (exit-127-style Err) rather than the refusal naming allowDegrade. Cosmetic ordering inconsistency vs foreground exec (which reports refusal first). Minor.

7. Now the BIGGER issue I want to verify — `updateSpec` on the SHELL vs the shell being recreated by the env's `updateSpec`. In `SandboxedExecutionEnv.updateSpec`, a NEW `SandboxedShell` is constructed each call, and the shell constructor calls `updateSpec(spec)` internally. For the allowDegrade path, `onDegrade` fires AT CONSTRUCTION — announcing "running in policy mode" once per updateSpec. If the CLI updates the same spec repeatedly (e.g. `/cube reload`), onDegrade fires each time — acceptable "loud" behavior.

8. `identityHashCode(this)` in tmp names: `identityHashCode` can be negative? In Dart, identityHashCode returns a non-negative int? Actually it can return any int32 value including negative? The docs: "Returns a hash code derived from the identity of the object" — value is an int, typically positive but not guaranteed. Path with `-` is fine anyway.

But hmm — what about `readTextFile` on a DIRECTORY (if a prisoner somehow made profilePath a directory)? readTextFile errors → restage → writeFile(tmp) ok → renamePath(tmp, profilePath) → on POSIX rename over a non-empty directory fails (ENOTEMPTY / EISDIR). Then stagingError set → refused exec. Fail closed. Good.

Actually `final tmp = '$profilePath.${identityHashCode(this)}-${_tmpSeq++}.tmp';` is synchronous — sequential within one isolate. Both execs get different tmp names. Both rename to profilePath — last wins, same content. Fine. Collision risk negligible for profile files, and content is verified before every exec anyway (readTextFile compare). Even on collision, the content check catches mismatch and restages — but wait, if two DIFFERENT specs' profiles collide in name, each exec would restage the file before each exec (they'd thrash but stay correct). 64-bit collisions are effectively impossible. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failed rename leaks the temp profile file**

When `writeFile(tmp)` succeeds but `renamePath(tmp, profilePath)` fails, the
`.tmp` file is left behind and never cleaned up; the next attempt derives a new
name via `_tmpSeq++`, so repeated staging failures (e.g. a read-only staging
directory that intermittently accepts writes, or a planted directory at
`profilePath` making every rename fail with `EISDIR`/`ENOTEMPTY`) accumulate
`~/.fah/cube-profiles/<hash>.<id>-<n>.tmp` files indefinitely.

Consider deleting the temp file (or reusing the same temp name) on the rename
failure path:

```dart
if (rename.isErr) {
  await fs.remove(tmp, force: true); // best-effort cleanup
  stagingError = 'profile staging failed: ${rename.errorOrNull!.message}';
  return false;
}
```

Pure hygiene — the fail-closed semantics are correct as written.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 815
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/815
- **Title**: fix(cube): backend kernel means kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit allowDegrade (#793)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-793` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +780
- **Deletions**: -150
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:58:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T23:13:13Z

## PR Description

## SEC-05 - `backend: kernel` is kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit `allowDegrade`

Closes #793. Stacked on #803 (SEC-02, same subsystem).

### Before
A `backend: kernel` spec on a host without an enforcing backend (Windows, web, Linux without user namespaces) **silently degraded to policy mode** - the requested isolation level was a wish, not a contract.

### After
- **Refuse by default.** Undeliverable kernel spec -> every `exec` and every background job answers a clean, stable `fa_cube[<name>]: backend: kernel is not available on this platform ... set spec.allowDegrade: true to allow the degrade` error. **Zero commands run**, zero staging writes, no wrapper is ever reached.
- **Explicit degrade.** `allowDegrade: true` in the manifest is the only path to policy mode; it fires `onDegrade` (loud `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unavailable, running in policy mode`), and the effective mode is queryable afterwards via `SandboxedShell.effectiveBackend` / `SandboxedExecutionEnv.effectiveBackend` (`null` = passthrough or refused; `policy` = degradaded or default; `kernel` = OS-wrapped).
- **Launch failures are not degrade.** A missing `sandbox-exec`/`unshare` or an EPERM/SBPL refusal on an *enforcing* platform stays a hard spawn error regardless of `allowDegrade` - the opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case.
- **Config surface.** `CubeSpec.allowDegrade` (default `false`), strict boolean parse, canonical map omits it when `false` (cache keys byte-identical), `schema/cube_schema.json` + `docs/cubes.md` document it; docs gain the platform x spec x fallback matrix.

### Acceptance (issue #793)
- **AC1** `kernel_spec_on_unsupported_platform_is_refused` - `test/cube/runtime/sandboxed_shell_test.dart` AC1 tests (windows / no-os / no-home: refusal names allowDegrade, inner shell never reached) + env-level background-job refusal.
- **AC2** `allow_degrade_runs_queryable` - AC2 test: degrading spec runs in policy mode, `onDegrade` fired, `effectiveBackend() == policy`; forward test on the env.
- **AC3** REG property test - AC3 "explicit kernel never silently executes in policy mode" across the os x allowDegrade matrix (macos/linux/windows/null): every outcome is kernel-wrapped, refused-with-reason, or explicitly-degraded-and-loud.
- Docs matrix: `docs/cubes.md` "spec.backend" (platform x spec -> kernel/policy/refusal).

`dart analyze lib/src/cube test/cube` clean; `test/cube` green apart from the 3 pre-existing live-leg failures proven identical on the pristine base (see #803): 315 passed / 3 skipped.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/cube_docs_linux_userns_matrix.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: docs matrix misstates the shipped behavior for "Linux (no user namespaces)"**

This row (and the prose at `docs/cubes.md:224-226`, which lists "Linux without
user namespaces" among "hosts without an enforcing backend") does not match the
implementation:

- `LinuxUnshareBackend.enforces` is statically `true` (`linux_unshare.dart:44`)
  and `osName` is always `Platform.operatingSystem` — there is no user-namespace
  capability probe. On a userns-less Linux host, `backend: kernel` **binds the
  kernel run** and every exec hard-fails as a launch failure
  (`fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unshare failed: ...`), not the clean
  "backend: kernel is not available on this platform … set spec.allowDegrade"
  refusal this row promises.
- Worse, the `+ allowDegrade: true` cell — "policy (+ loud warning)" — cannot
  happen: `allowDegrade` only applies when `_kernelRunFor` returns null
  (`sandboxed_shell.dart:203-214`), and on Linux it never does. The PR's own
  description states the correct rule ("launch failures are not degrade … the
  opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case"); the table contradicts
  both the code and the PR prose.

An operator on a userns-less Linux CI container (common, per the test note in
`linux_unshare.dart`) reading this matrix would expect `allowDegrade: true` to
yield a working policy-mode run; instead every command errors. Since the
platform × spec × fallback matrix is an explicit AC of this PR, please fix
before merge — either:

1. correct the row/prose to "hard error (unshare EPERM) — launch failures are
   never degraded, even with `allowDegrade: true`", or
2. make the docs true by adding a user-namespace capability probe so a
   userns-less Linux really refuses (clean `allowDegrade`-naming error) /
   degrades under the opt-in.

Option 1 is the minimal fix consistent with the stated design rule; option 2
changes runtime behavior and deserves its own issue.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/cube_preset_refuse_no_optin.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: builtin presets have no `allowDegrade` escape hatch — on Windows/web every preset now refuses all commands**

Every builtin preset generates `backend: kernel` with no `allowDegrade`
(`cube_presets.dart:150`), and there is no CLI surface to opt in
(`/cube use <preset>` → `maybeSpec` builds the manifest verbatim). With the new
kernel-or-refuse rule created at this line, a preset user on Windows, web, or
any host without an enforcing backend (or without `HOME` set) goes from
"works in policy mode with a loud warning" (previous behavior) to **every
command refused** — the only remedy is hand-writing a custom manifest that
duplicates the preset and adds `allowDegrade: true`.

The hardening itself is right (SEC-05), but the opt-in the refusal message
recommends (`set spec.allowDegrade: true`) is unreachable for preset users.
Please address at least one of:

1. Document the preset consequence in `docs/cubes.md`'s preset section (the new
   matrix doesn't mention presets at all) and in the refusal path when the
   active spec came from a preset.
2. Add a first-class opt-in: a preset variant (e.g. `l1-core-degrade`), a
   `/cube use <preset> --allow-degrade` flag, or a generated-manifest override
   — so the fix the error message names is actually available.

Also worth noting: `SandboxedShell.prepare` changed `Future<String>` →
`Future<String?>` and the refusal/passthrough semantics are new; both are
public API via `lib/src/cube/cube.dart` — fine for this repo, but worth a line
in the release notes since external hosts may call `prepare()` directly.
"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failed rename leaks the temp profile file**

When `writeFile(tmp)` succeeds but `renamePath(tmp, profilePath)` fails, the
`.tmp` file is left behind and never cleaned up; the next attempt derives a new
name via `_tmpSeq++`, so repeated staging failures (e.g. a read-only staging
directory that intermittently accepts writes, or a planted directory at
`profilePath` making every rename fail with `EISDIR`/`ENOTEMPTY`) accumulate
`~/.fah/cube-profiles/<hash>.<id>-<n>.tmp` files indefinitely.

Consider deleting the temp file (or reusing the same temp name) on the rename
failure path:

```dart
if (rename.isErr) {
  await fs.remove(tmp, force: true); // best-effort cleanup
  stagingError = 'profile staging failed: ${rename.errorOrNull!.message}';
  return false;
}
```

Pure hygiene — the fail-closed semantics are correct as written.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/cube_staging_tmp_leak.md"}

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-793` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +780
- **Deletions**: -150
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:58:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T23:13:13Z

## PR Description

## SEC-05 - `backend: kernel` is kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit `allowDegrade`

Closes #793. Stacked on #803 (SEC-02, same subsystem).

### Before
A `backend: kernel` spec on a host without an enforcing backend (Windows, web, Linux without user namespaces) **silently degraded to policy mode** - the requested isolation level was a wish, not a contract.

### After
- **Refuse by default.** Undeliverable kernel spec -> every `exec` and every background job answers a clean, stable `fa_cube[<name>]: backend: kernel is not available on this platform ... set spec.allowDegrade: true to allow the degrade` error. **Zero commands run**, zero staging writes, no wrapper is ever reached.
- **Explicit degrade.** `allowDegrade: true` in the manifest is the only path to policy mode; it fires `onDegrade` (loud `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unavailable, running in policy mode`), and the effective mode is queryable afterwards via `SandboxedShell.effectiveBackend` / `SandboxedExecutionEnv.effectiveBackend` (`null` = passthrough or refused; `policy` = degradaded or default; `kernel` = OS-wrapped).
- **Launch failures are not degrade.** A missing `sandbox-exec`/`unshare` or an EPERM/SBPL refusal on an *enforcing* platform stays a hard spawn error regardless of `allowDegrade` - the opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case.
- **Config surface.** `CubeSpec.allowDegrade` (default `false`), strict boolean parse, canonical map omits it when `false` (cache keys byte-identical), `schema/cube_schema.json` + `docs/cubes.md` document it; docs gain the platform x spec x fallback matrix.

### Acceptance (issue #793)
- **AC1** `kernel_spec_on_unsupported_platform_is_refused` - `test/cube/runtime/sandboxed_shell_test.dart` AC1 tests (windows / no-os / no-home: refusal names allowDegrade, inner shell never reached) + env-level background-job refusal.
- **AC2** `allow_degrade_runs_queryable` - AC2 test: degrading spec runs in policy mode, `onDegrade` fired, `effectiveBackend() == policy`; forward test on the env.
- **AC3** REG property test - AC3 "explicit kernel never silently executes in policy mode" across the os x allowDegrade matrix (macos/linux/windows/null): every outcome is kernel-wrapped, refused-with-reason, or explicitly-degraded-and-loud.
- Docs matrix: `docs/cubes.md` "spec.backend" (platform x spec -> kernel/policy/refusal).

`dart analyze lib/src/cube test/cube` clean; `test/cube` green apart from the 3 pre-existing live-leg failures proven identical on the pristine base (see #803): 315 passed / 3 skipped.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failed rename leaks the temp profile file**

When `writeFile(tmp)` succeeds but `renamePath(tmp, profilePath)` fails, the
`.tmp` file is left behind and never cleaned up; the next attempt derives a new
name via `_tmpSeq++`, so repeated staging failures (e.g. a read-only staging
directory that intermittently accepts writes, or a planted directory at
`profilePath` making every rename fail with `EISDIR`/`ENOTEMPTY`) accumulate
`~/.fah/cube-profiles/<hash>.<id>-<n>.tmp` files indefinitely.

Consider deleting the temp file (or reusing the same temp name) on the rename
failure path:

```dart
if (rename.isErr) {
  await fs.remove(tmp, force: true); // best-effort cleanup
  stagingError = 'profile staging failed: ${rename.errorOrNull!.message}';
  return false;
}
```

Pure hygiene — the fail-closed semantics are correct as written.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 815
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/815
- **Title**: fix(cube): backend kernel means kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit allowDegrade (#793)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-793` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +780
- **Deletions**: -150
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:58:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T23:13:13Z

## PR Description

## SEC-05 - `backend: kernel` is kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit `allowDegrade`

Closes #793. Stacked on #803 (SEC-02, same subsystem).

### Before
A `backend: kernel` spec on a host without an enforcing backend (Windows, web, Linux without user namespaces) **silently degraded to policy mode** - the requested isolation level was a wish, not a contract.

### After
- **Refuse by default.** Undeliverable kernel spec -> every `exec` and every background job answers a clean, stable `fa_cube[<name>]: backend: kernel is not available on this platform ... set spec.allowDegrade: true to allow the degrade` error. **Zero commands run**, zero staging writes, no wrapper is ever reached.
- **Explicit degrade.** `allowDegrade: true` in the manifest is the only path to policy mode; it fires `onDegrade` (loud `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unavailable, running in policy mode`), and the effective mode is queryable afterwards via `SandboxedShell.effectiveBackend` / `SandboxedExecutionEnv.effectiveBackend` (`null` = passthrough or refused; `policy` = degradaded or default; `kernel` = OS-wrapped).
- **Launch failures are not degrade.** A missing `sandbox-exec`/`unshare` or an EPERM/SBPL refusal on an *enforcing* platform stays a hard spawn error regardless of `allowDegrade` - the opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case.
- **Config surface.** `CubeSpec.allowDegrade` (default `false`), strict boolean parse, canonical map omits it when `false` (cache keys byte-identical), `schema/cube_schema.json` + `docs/cubes.md` document it; docs gain the platform x spec x fallback matrix.

### Acceptance (issue #793)
- **AC1** `kernel_spec_on_unsupported_platform_is_refused` - `test/cube/runtime/sandboxed_shell_test.dart` AC1 tests (windows / no-os / no-home: refusal names allowDegrade, inner shell never reached) + env-level background-job refusal.
- **AC2** `allow_degrade_runs_queryable` - AC2 test: degrading spec runs in policy mode, `onDegrade` fired, `effectiveBackend() == policy`; forward test on the env.
- **AC3** REG property test - AC3 "explicit kernel never silently executes in policy mode" across the os x allowDegrade matrix (macos/linux/windows/null): every outcome is kernel-wrapped, refused-with-reason, or explicitly-degraded-and-loud.
- Docs matrix: `docs/cubes.md` "spec.backend" (platform x spec -> kernel/policy/refusal).

`dart analyze lib/src/cube test/cube` clean; `test/cube` green apart from the 3 pre-existing live-leg failures proven identical on the pristine base (see #803): 315 passed / 3 skipped.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

2. Behavior when spec is `policy` but with `allowDegrade: true` — the `_kernelRunFor` returns null because backend != kernel; `updateSpec` only fires onDegrade when `spec.backend == kernel`. So allowDegrade with policy backend is silently accepted — fine (no-op).

But NOTE: two specs, one with allowDegrade:false explicitly in the map... parse drops the distinction — canonical map only includes allowDegrade when true. So `backend: kernel` + `allowDegrade: false` == `backend: kernel` alone. Byte-identical keys. Intended.

4. IMPORTANT — potential issue in `exec()` ordering: For a REFUSED spec, exec returns Err BEFORE the policy check. So even a policy-DENIED command returns the refusal error instead of the standard exit-127 `Ok` result. This is intentional per PR description ("every exec ... answers a clean, stable error"). OK.

5. Now a REAL potential correctness issue: `startupFailure()` when `kernel != null` and probed — `if (kernel.probed) return kernel.failureNote;`. First call: `kernel.probed = true; if (!await kernel.stageVerified()) {...}`. Then it runs the wrapped `true` probe through `_inner.exec` — that RUNS A COMMAND (`sandbox-exec -f profile true`). But wait — the startup probe runs `kernel.backend.wrapCommand('true', ...)` — the raw wrapped `true` command, executed via `_inner.exec` WITHOUT the policy engine check. This is a hard-coded `true` no-op, fine by design (documented "runs a wrapped no-op command once per spec first").

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: `startupFailure()` doesn't check `_refusal` before `kernel.probed` — it does: refusal checked before kernel. Good.

6. Another potential issue: in `SandboxedExecutionEnv.startShellJob`, for a refused spec the policy check runs first: `engine.checkCommand(command)`.
