{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/cube_docs_linux_userns_matrix.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: docs matrix misstates the shipped behavior for "Linux (no user namespaces)"**

This row (and the prose at `docs/cubes.md:224-226`, which lists "Linux without
user namespaces" among "hosts without an enforcing backend") does not match the
implementation:

- `LinuxUnshareBackend.enforces` is statically `true` (`linux_unshare.dart:44`)
  and `osName` is always `Platform.operatingSystem` — there is no user-namespace
  capability probe. On a userns-less Linux host, `backend: kernel` **binds the
  kernel run** and every exec hard-fails as a launch failure
  (`fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unshare failed: ...`), not the clean
  "backend: kernel is not available on this platform … set spec.allowDegrade"
  refusal this row promises.
- Worse, the `+ allowDegrade: true` cell — "policy (+ loud warning)" — cannot
  happen: `allowDegrade` only applies when `_kernelRunFor` returns null
  (`sandboxed_shell.dart:203-214`), and on Linux it never does. The PR's own
  description states the correct rule ("launch failures are not degrade … the
  opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case"); the table contradicts
  both the code and the PR prose.

An operator on a userns-less Linux CI container (common, per the test note in
`linux_unshare.dart`) reading this matrix would expect `allowDegrade: true` to
yield a working policy-mode run; instead every command errors. Since the
platform × spec × fallback matrix is an explicit AC of this PR, please fix
before merge — either:

1. correct the row/prose to "hard error (unshare EPERM) — launch failures are
   never degraded, even with `allowDegrade: true`", or
2. make the docs true by adding a user-namespace capability probe so a
   userns-less Linux really refuses (clean `allowDegrade`-naming error) /
   degrades under the opt-in.

Option 1 is the minimal fix consistent with the stated design rule; option 2
changes runtime behavior and deserves its own issue.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/cube_preset_refuse_no_optin.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: builtin presets have no `allowDegrade` escape hatch — on Windows/web every preset now refuses all commands**

Every builtin preset generates `backend: kernel` with no `allowDegrade`
(`cube_presets.dart:150`), and there is no CLI surface to opt in
(`/cube use <preset>` → `maybeSpec` builds the manifest verbatim). With the new
kernel-or-refuse rule created at this line, a preset user on Windows, web, or
any host without an enforcing backend (or without `HOME` set) goes from
"works in policy mode with a loud warning" (previous behavior) to **every
command refused** — the only remedy is hand-writing a custom manifest that
duplicates the preset and adds `allowDegrade: true`.

The hardening itself is right (SEC-05), but the opt-in the refusal message
recommends (`set spec.allowDegrade: true`) is unreachable for preset users.
Please address at least one of:

1. Document the preset consequence in `docs/cubes.md`'s preset section (the new
   matrix doesn't mention presets at all) and in the refusal path when the
   active spec came from a preset.
2. Add a first-class opt-in: a preset variant (e.g. `l1-core-degrade`), a
   `/cube use <preset> --allow-degrade` flag, or a generated-manifest override
   — so the fix the error message names is actually available.

Also worth noting: `SandboxedShell.prepare` changed `Future<String>` →
`Future<String?>` and the refusal/passthrough semantics are new; both are
public API via `lib/src/cube/cube.dart` — fine for this repo, but worth a line
in the release notes since external hosts may call `prepare()` directly.
"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failed rename leaks the temp profile file**

When `writeFile(tmp)` succeeds but `renamePath(tmp, profilePath)` fails, the
`.tmp` file is left behind and never cleaned up; the next attempt derives a new
name via `_tmpSeq++`, so repeated staging failures (e.g. a read-only staging
directory that intermittently accepts writes, or a planted directory at
`profilePath` making every rename fail with `EISDIR`/`ENOTEMPTY`) accumulate
`~/.fah/cube-profiles/<hash>.<id>-<n>.tmp` files indefinitely.

Consider deleting the temp file (or reusing the same temp name) on the rename
failure path:

```dart
if (rename.isErr) {
  await fs.remove(tmp, force: true); // best-effort cleanup
  stagingError = 'profile staging failed: ${rename.errorOrNull!.message}';
  return false;
}
```

Pure hygiene — the fail-closed semantics are correct as written.

- **PR #**: 815
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/815
- **Title**: fix(cube): backend kernel means kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit allowDegrade (#793)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-793` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +780
- **Deletions**: -150
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:58:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T23:13:13Z

## PR Description

## SEC-05 - `backend: kernel` is kernel-or-refuse, degrade only via explicit `allowDegrade`

Closes #793. Stacked on #803 (SEC-02, same subsystem).

### Before
A `backend: kernel` spec on a host without an enforcing backend (Windows, web, Linux without user namespaces) **silently degraded to policy mode** - the requested isolation level was a wish, not a contract.

### After
- **Refuse by default.** Undeliverable kernel spec -> every `exec` and every background job answers a clean, stable `fa_cube[<name>]: backend: kernel is not available on this platform ... set spec.allowDegrade: true to allow the degrade` error. **Zero commands run**, zero staging writes, no wrapper is ever reached.
- **Explicit degrade.** `allowDegrade: true` in the manifest is the only path to policy mode; it fires `onDegrade` (loud `fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unavailable, running in policy mode`), and the effective mode is queryable afterwards via `SandboxedShell.effectiveBackend` / `SandboxedExecutionEnv.effectiveBackend` (`null` = passthrough or refused; `policy` = degradaded or default; `kernel` = OS-wrapped).
- **Launch failures are not degrade.** A missing `sandbox-exec`/`unshare` or an EPERM/SBPL refusal on an *enforcing* platform stays a hard spawn error regardless of `allowDegrade` - the opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case.
- **Config surface.** `CubeSpec.allowDegrade` (default `false`), strict boolean parse, canonical map omits it when `false` (cache keys byte-identical), `schema/cube_schema.json` + `docs/cubes.md` document it; docs gain the platform x spec x fallback matrix.

### Acceptance (issue #793)
- **AC1** `kernel_spec_on_unsupported_platform_is_refused` - `test/cube/runtime/sandboxed_shell_test.dart` AC1 tests (windows / no-os / no-home: refusal names allowDegrade, inner shell never reached) + env-level background-job refusal.
- **AC2** `allow_degrade_runs_queryable` - AC2 test: degrading spec runs in policy mode, `onDegrade` fired, `effectiveBackend() == policy`; forward test on the env.
- **AC3** REG property test - AC3 "explicit kernel never silently executes in policy mode" across the os x allowDegrade matrix (macos/linux/windows/null): every outcome is kernel-wrapped, refused-with-reason, or explicitly-degraded-and-loud.
- Docs matrix: `docs/cubes.md` "spec.backend" (platform x spec -> kernel/policy/refusal).

`dart analyze lib/src/cube test/cube` clean; `test/cube` green apart from the 3 pre-existing live-leg failures proven identical on the pristine base (see #803): 315 passed / 3 skipped.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside

  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap

  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`

So even a policy-DENIED command returns the refusal error instead of the standard exit-127 `Ok` result. This is intentional per PR description ("every exec ... answers a clean, stable error"). OK.

5. Now a REAL potential correctness issue: `startupFailure()` when `kernel != null` and probed — `if (kernel.probed) return kernel.failureNote;`. First call: `kernel.probed = true; if (!await kernel.stageVerified()) {...}`. Then it runs the wrapped `true` probe through `_inner.exec` — that RUNS A COMMAND (`sandbox-exec -f profile true`). But wait — the startup probe runs `kernel.backend.wrapCommand('true', ...)` — the raw wrapped `true` command, executed via `_inner.exec` WITHOUT the policy engine check. This is a hard-coded `true` no-op, fine by design (documented "runs a wrapped no-op command once per spec first").

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: `startupFailure()` doesn't check `_refusal` before `kernel.probed` — it does: refusal checked before kernel. Good.

In `SandboxedExecutionEnv.updateSpec`, a NEW `SandboxedShell` is constructed each call, and the shell constructor calls `updateSpec(spec)` internally. Then stagingError set → refused exec. Fail closed. Good.

This row (and the prose at `docs/cubes.md:224-226`, which lists "Linux without
user namespaces" among "hosts without an enforcing backend") does not match the
implementation:

- `LinuxUnshareBackend.enforces` is statically `true` (`linux_unshare.dart:44`)
  and `osName` is always `Platform.operatingSystem` — there is no user-namespace
  capability probe. On a userns-less Linux host, `backend: kernel` **binds the
  kernel run** and every exec hard-fails as a launch failure
  (`fa_cube[<name>]: kernel backend unshare failed: ...`), not the clean
  "backend: kernel is not available on this platform … set spec.allowDegrade"
  refusal this row promises.
- Worse, the `+ allowDegrade: true` cell — "policy (+ loud warning)" — cannot
  happen: `allowDegrade` only applies when `_kernelRunFor` returns null
  (`sandboxed_shell.dart:203-214`), and on Linux it never does. The PR's own
  description states the correct rule ("launch failures are not degrade … the
  opt-in only covers the no-backend-for-platform case"); the table contradicts
  both the code and the PR prose.

An operator on a userns-less Linux CI container (common, per the test note in
`linux_unshare.dart`) reading this matrix would expect `allowDegrade: true` to
yield a working policy-mode run; instead every command errors. Since the
platform × spec × fallback matrix is an explicit AC of this PR, please fix
before merge — either:

1. correct the row/prose to "hard error (unshare EPERM) — launch failures are
   never degraded, even with `allowDegrade: true`", or
2. make the docs true by adding a user-namespace capability probe so a
   userns-less Linux really refuses (clean `allowDegrade`-naming error) /
   degrades under the opt-in.

Option 1 is the minimal fix consistent with the stated design rule; option 2
changes runtime behavior and deserves its own issue.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/cube_preset_refuse_no_optin.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: builtin presets have no `allowDegrade` escape hatch — on Windows/web every preset now refuses all commands**

Every builtin preset generates `backend: kernel` with no `allowDegrade`
(`cube_presets.dart:150`), and there is no CLI surface to opt in
(`/cube use <preset>` → `maybeSpec` builds the manifest verbatim). With the new
kernel-or-refuse rule created at this line, a preset user on Windows, web, or
any host without an enforcing backend (or without `HOME` set) goes from
"works in policy mode with a loud warning" (previous behavior) to **every
command refused** — the only remedy is hand-writing a custom manifest that
duplicates the preset and adds `allowDegrade: true`.

The hardening itself is right (SEC-05), but the opt-in the refusal message
recommends (`set spec.allowDegrade: true`) is unreachable for preset users.
Please address at least one of:

1. Document the preset consequence in `docs/cubes.md`'s preset section (the new
   matrix doesn't mention presets at all) and in the refusal path when the
   active spec came from a preset.
2. Add a first-class opt-in: a preset variant (e.g. `l1-core-degrade`), a
   `/cube use <preset> --allow-degrade` flag, or a generated-manifest override
   — so the fix the error message names is actually available.

Also worth noting: `SandboxedShell.prepare` changed `Future<String>` →
`Future<String?>` and the refusal/passthrough semantics are new; both are
public API via `lib/src/cube/cube.dart` — fine for this repo, but worth a line
in the release notes since external hosts may call `prepare()` directly.
"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failed rename leaks the temp profile file**

When `writeFile(tmp)` succeeds but `renamePath(tmp, profilePath)` fails, the
`.tmp` file is left behind and never cleaned up; the next attempt derives a new
name via `_tmpSeq++`, so repeated staging failures (e.g. a read-only staging
directory that intermittently accepts writes, or a planted directory at
`profilePath` making every rename fail with `EISDIR`/`ENOTEMPTY`) accumulate
`~/.fah/cube-profiles/<hash>.<id>-<n>.tmp` files indefinitely.

Consider deleting the temp file (or reusing the same temp name) on the rename
failure path:

```dart
if (rename.isErr) {
  await fs.remove(tmp, force: true); // best-effort cleanup
  stagingError = 'profile staging failed: ${rename.errorOrNull!.message}';
  return false;
}
```

Pure hygiene — the fail-closed semantics are correct as written.
